description: Keeps the main thread thin: a clearly multi-step / implementation-shaped Bash by the orchestrator (chained >2 steps, a heredoc, sed -i/tee, npm/cargo/make build, git commit/push, pytest/test runs, AND all `gh` incl. `gh ship`/`gh pr`/`gh run`/`gh api`) warns-then-blocks. A bare >/>> redirect is not implementation on its own. Read-only inspection AND sanctioned orchestration are never blocked, even chained: git status/ls/cat/grep/find, tg, review, git worktree list. One narrow, multiply-gated heredoc exception (agent-tools#307): `$(cat <<'DELIM' ...DELIM)` (quoted delimiter, bare `cat`, no extra file arg) collapses to a plain string ONLY when it is ALSO a plain argument that starts a genuinely SEPARATE shell word (no redirect operator -- `>`, `>&`, `>|`, or word/quote-concatenated -- and no `#` comment ANYWHERE in the current segment, not just immediately adjacent; no backslash, `$'` (ANSI-C quote), or bare grouping/arithmetic `(` anywhere in the segment either, since any of these defeats bracket/quote counting) of an already-`tg`-headed segment (EXACT token match, not a `tg` prefix like `tg-ctl`; wrapper-stripped: `timeout`/`env`/`VAR=val` prefixes still qualify; narrower than the general orchestration allow-list -- `git worktree list`/`review` do not carve out a heredoc argument) at substitution depth 0, OUTSIDE any open top-level single-quote, and the substitution itself wrapped in double quotes (an unquoted `$(...)` is subject to bash's own word-splitting/globbing, which can turn a single heredoc body into multiple CLI-flag-shaped argv elements), with quote/comment state tracked PER SUBSTITUTION NESTING LEVEL via its own stack (each $(...)/<(/>(/bare `(` pushes an independent scope and its matching `)` pops back to the parent's, so an earlier heredoc's own body content does not desync a later segment's head match via the nested-substitution-quoting class of bypass this stack was built to close (a QUOTED paren inside a nested substitution no longer drops depth early) -- this is NOT an absolute guarantee against every possible cross-body interference, though: a stray UNMATCHED quote character sitting inside an earlier heredoc's own body can still, in rare cases, widen or narrow a LATER sibling segment's head match, a known, tested, safe-direction-only residual (over-blocks, never launders anything) documented in the README and pinned by a dedicated regression test rather than fixed, since properly closing it would require making the mask heredoc-body-aware, a larger change; a backtick ` `` ` also pushes a scope but is INCREMENT-ONLY -- never popped, since bash's own closing token is another backtick, not a distinguishable character -- so a properly-paired earlier `` `cmd` `` permanently raises depth and over-blocks a later, otherwise-safe heredoc in the same command; a known, safe-direction accepted bias, not a bug) -- everything else (unquoted delimiter, non-cat consumer, nested substitution, redirect-to-file, comment-hidden fake heredoc, eval/bash -c/source or any other non-sanctioned head) still hits the blanket heredoc block. ALL `gh` is DELEGATED to a subagent now (Alex tg#7103, reverting the #159/#162 gh-ship carve-out): shipping (`gh ship`) and CI/PR verification (`gh pr checks/view`, `gh run`, `gh api`) are a subagent's job, not inline orchestrator work. Subagent commands (agent_id present) are allowed. WARN first, BLOCK on repeat within ORCH_THIN_TTL_S (900s). Per-repo opt-out (repo owner, not the constrained agent): agent_hooks.orchestrator_only:false in rig.yaml or RIG_ORCHESTRATOR_ONLY=0 (default ON). Deny-by-default: no self-service bypass (ALLOW_ORCHESTRATOR_WORK env / `# orchestrator-ok:` sentinel removed); a would-be BLOCK consults RIG_HATCH_REQUEST_ORCHESTRATOR_STAYS_THIN with a written justification, which asks Telegram via trusted tg-ctl and allows ONLY on an approval tap (a blank/bare 1 denies). timeout_ms 960000 covers tg-ctl ask's 900s cap plus margin so a hung/unanswered ask can't race the dispatcher's descriptor-timeout kill into a silent on_error=open ALLOW; a CC settings entry launching cc_hook_bridge must set timeout >960s (the 600s CC default would preempt this). on_error=open.
